_comment: Command-name sets for the bash guard. Single source of truth consumed by the shared core (~/.agents/guardrails/core.ts), used by Claude and pi via their adapters. Data only — the logic lives in core.ts. See README.md. Add a dangerous command here once; all agents pick it up.
_destructive_prefixes: Matched with startsWith, because the filesystem-maker family is open-ended: enumerating ten mkfs.* names still missed mkfs.f2fs and mkfs.exfat, and the next new filesystem reopens the hole with no symptom.
_host_control: Powering the workstation off or rebooting it is never the agent's call, and it ends the session mid-task.
_network_fetchers: Only meaningful piped into a bare shell -- see remote-code. A fetcher on its own is ordinary work.
_scratch_roots: The session scratch directory, and only that. A recursive rm STRICTLY BELOW it is allowed without prompting: the ask tier exists because agent-checkpoint cannot recover the target, and for a scratch tree that is the point of the directory rather than a loss. /tmp is deliberately NOT here -- project checkouts and agent worktrees holding uncommitted work live under it. The root itself is never exempt either.
_find_policy: per-agent find handling (gate severity is 'ask'; each adapter maps that to a prompt or a block): 'always' = gate any find; 'exec' = gate only when an -exec/-delete primary is present; 'off' = ignore.
_severity: recursive-force-rm is ASK for every agent since 2026-09-08: the allow tier rested on agent-checkpoint covering the target, and a checkpoint never captures gitignored trees because git add -A honours .gitignore -- so build outputs, caches and results/ were never in a snapshot. Per-category decision for command rules. A string applies to every agent; an object keys by agent like find_policy. An unlisted category resolves to 'ask', so this is fail-safe.
